data.abstract: The rise of cyberbullying has become increasingly concerning with the widespread adoption of technology. This study investigated the relationship between cyberbullying and emotional intelligence among adolescents in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. A quantitative approach was conducted, with data collected from 550 students through an online questionnaire. The results revealed a significant negative relationship between cyberbullying and emotional intelligence among adolescents. These findings carry important implications for educators, parents, and policymakers. Addressing cyberbullying is crucial not only for safeguarding students' emotional well-being but also for promoting the development of emotional intelligence. Efforts should focus on raising awareness, providing emotional support, and creating robust anti-bullying strategies to mitigate the adverse effects of cyberbullying on students' emotional development.
title: Exploring the Impact of Cyberbullying on Emotional Intelligence among Saudi Adolescents

data.abstract: <jats:p>Cyberbullying among adolescents in India presents a pressing yet inadequately understood public health concern. In the present systematic review, a comprehensive search across 6 electronic databases (PsycINFO, Embase, MEDLINE, ERIC, Web of Science, and PubMed) in September 2024 yielded 1,332 articles, of which 46 met full inclusion criteria. Cyberbullying victimization rates ranged from 2.7% to 72%, and perpetration from 3% to 34.9%, reflecting substantial regional and methodological heterogeneity. Common forms included impersonation, harassment, denigration, exclusion, and severe digital violence. Risk factors identified were age, female gender, personality traits such as narcissism and callousness, limited parental monitoring, and prolonged social media use, while consequences included depression, suicidal ideation, and reduced self-esteem. Only one intervention study was identified, underscoring a critical gap. Methodologically, most studies relied on convenience sampling, self-report measures unvalidated for Indian populations, and basic statistical analyses, limiting generalizability. Future research should prioritize culturally validated instruments, representative sampling, longitudinal designs, and evidence-based interventions contextually adapted to India&apos;s sociocultural diversity.</jats:p>
title: Cyberbullying among Adolescents in India: A Systematic Review

data.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Cyberbullying is commonly present as affecting in adolescent population. Current research suggests that cyberbullying occurs mostly in secondary education. There was a total of 186 students who participated in this study. It was found that there was a significant association between cyberbullying and cyber victimization which suggest that cyber victims have the tendency to be cyberbullies and vice versa. Moreover, more than half of the victims do not report cyberbullying phenomena to adults. It was also found out that schools were the least medium for adolescent to learn safety strategies online.</jats:p>

data.abstract: <jats:p>Cyberbullying is a form of bullying or harassing which is done by sending aggressive messages to a person. It can be a humiliating photo or video, an unpleasant text message, or an intolerable comment on social media. Cyberbullying has divided into two types like Direct and Indirect cyberbullying. Direct cyberbullying is sending harmful material in the form of text, image, etc., to torture the victim directly. Indirect cyberbullying is when someone spreads the rumor about another person's life. In the existing technique, Direct and Indirect cyberbullying Identification of User Character (IUC), Identification of Trustworthiness of the User (ITU) are detected using classifiers techniques from the Twitter dataset. This proposed technique is going to detect cyberbullying from direct, indirect cyberbullying techniques and to prevent the cyberbullying by reflective messages and also to recover the victims using depression technique. Along with existing technique, this proposed technique is going to detect depression from the cyberbully affected persons in order to recover from their depressive mood. The depression can be detected by using the following techniques, namely, Cognitive distortions, Depressive rumination, Content valence and Attitude towards others. This proposed technique also reduces the cyber harassment by showing the reflective messages to the harassing persons. The reflective message helps the users to reconsider and it prevents them from posting harmful messages. The reflective message is going to detect from the following techniques such as the potential audience, Disapproval by bystanders and Harm for the receiver.</jats:p>
title: Cyberbullying Among Adolescents: An Effort Of Identification, Prevention and Intervention of Cyberbullying

data.abstract: <jats:p>Cyberbullying is on the rise so as its negative impact particularly on the health of the youth worldwide. While concerned about, the Governments and international research communities are growingly collaborating for publishing studies to highlight growing cluster of issues surrounding youth cyberbullying. In this regard, a Progressive Data Analysis (PDA) approach in conjunction with VOSviewer software was adopted for the collection and analysis of the cyberbullying publication data for the period of 2000 - 2021. The VOSviewer software helped to collect publication data from Scopus database and develop visuals whereas the PDA guided use to divide the dataset into four incremental time intervals (2000 – 2010, 2000 – 2015, 2000 – 2018 and 2000 - 2021) to effectively visualise the growing impact of cyberbullying on youth.</jats:p>
title: Growing Landscape of Cyberbullying Among Adolescents: An Analytical Approach to Two Decades of Research
